rationale:
Evidence: iteration 3 (score 396.3) is the best design so far. Its oval finish rate is 100% at 1.7 s mean, so the layout and turn rate work on gentle curves. The s-bend fails at progress 0.46 and the slalom at 0.09, both ending off track with max_error about 0.062 just above the 0.06 m limit. Body width is already at 0.18 m, which gives the maximum allowance (the limit is the 0.06 floor), so the fix has to come from control. Steering oscillation (0.18 oval, 0.30 s-bend) and RMS error are small, so the robot is not ringing. It is being pushed outward on tight alternating bends, which means it reacts too slowly or lacks authority. Slalom is the worst case: it fails within about 9% of the course, so the robot is probably entering the sharp direction changes at too high a speed. Iteration 2 moved sensor width, wheel track, speed and kp together, and that run was worse, so I keep the sensor layout and wheel track that worked best.

Changes: (1) base_speed 1.2 -> 1.05 to give more time to correct on slalom and s-bend bends. The oval mean time should rise from about 1.7 s to about 2.0 s, still within the 3 s limit, costing about 3 score points on the finish term. (2) kp 5.0 -> 5.5 for stronger correction of the outward drift. (3) kd 0.8 -> 1.0 to damp the higher kp, since the signal changes fast on alternating bends. (4) ki stays at 0.2 for the fixed motor mismatch. (5) Geometry is unchanged from iteration 3 (12 mm sensors at x = -0.03 to +0.03, y = 0.05, wheel track 0.10, mass 0.6), so the result isolates the speed and gain effect.

Expected result: s-bend progress above 0.6 and slalom progress above 0.3, with line_loss_events below 1 on both. Oval should still complete, at roughly 2.0 s. Hypotheses: (H1) lower speed is the main factor on slalom, so its progress should rise sharply as base_speed drops. (H2) kd 1.0 keeps steering_oscillation below about 0.4 with the higher kp. (H3) if oval completion falls below 1.0 or steering_oscillation exceeds 0.5, kp is too high and should drop to about 5.0. Measurements next: per-track completion, progress, max_error against the 0.06 limit, line_loss_events, and oval completion_time, to decide whether the next step is more speed or more gain.
